answer.question: Where is render_template used, and what breaks if I change it?
answer.text:
In short: render_template() converts template names into rendered HTML strings. It's used by 31 places across Flask—mainly route handlers that return templated pages—and changing it could break any view that displays dynamic content.

Where it lives: src/flask/templating.py:L136

Who depends on it: 31 places depend on it within 3 hops. The most critical are:

-
Route handlers in tutorial/blog.py and auth.py – Flask's own examples; if broken, the tutorial app won't load pages
-
Test apps in blueprintapp – Tests verify blueprint routing works; if broken, tests fail silently
-
Type checking tests (typing_route.py) – Ensures Flask's type hints are correct; breaking this catches signature bugs early
-
Core Flask exports (flask/__init__.py) – The public API; changes here affect every Flask user

If you change it:

-
Any route that calls render_template("mytemplate.html", data=value) will break
-
Template variable injection stops working (e.g., request, g, url_for won't be available in templates)
-
Run tests/test_views.py and tests/test_signals.py first—they directly test template rendering and context injection

Try this: Open src/flask/templating.py and look at the _render() function just above render_template() at L123 to see what it actually does. Then check one test: tests/test_signals.py::test_before_render_template shows what happens when a template renders.
